notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(14) The evergreen forests in India.

Ans. (1) The evergreen forests in India are found in the regions receiving abundant sunlight and annual average rainfall more than 2000 mm. These forests are found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Western Ghats, the coastline of peninsular India and the Assam region in the north-east.

(2) The trees like mahogany, rosewood, rubber, sandalwood, etc. are found in the evergreen forests in India. Various types of creepers are also found in these forests.

(3) The trees from evergreen forests have broad and green leaves. Their wood is found to be hard, heavy and durable.

(4) Many species of vegetation and wildlife is found in evergreen forests in India.

(15) Wildlife in India.

Ans. (1) India is gifted with rich and diversified wildlife. India is the only country in the world that has tigers as well as lions.

(2) Elephants are found in the hot and humid forests in the southern part of India. Assam is famous for one-horned rhinoceroses. They are found in swampy and marshy lands of Assam. Wild ass and camels are commonly found in arid desert lands in India. Snow leopards and yaks are found in the snow capped northern regions of Himalayan range.

(3) Indian bisons, deer, antelopes, monkeys are the animals seen in peninsular region of India. Turtles, crocodiles and gharials are seen in the rivers, estuaries and western and eastern coastal regions of India.

(4) Peacocks, Indian bustard, kingfishers, peasants, ducks, parakeets, cranes, pigeons, etc. are the major birds seen in various parts of India.

(16) Himalayan forests in India.

Ans. (1) The forests in Himalayan range are known as Himalayan forests. Himalayan forests are classified into three types on the basis of altitude.

(2) The areas at higher altitude in Himalayan range are often covered with snow. In summer, the snow from this region starts melting leading to growth of seasonal flowing trees.

(3) The areas at medium altitude in the Himalayan range are covered with the forests having the coniferous trees like pine, deodar, fir, etc. These trees have needle-shaped leaves. These leaves allows for snow to easily glide off the branches.

(4) The areas at low altitude in the Himalayan range, i.e. at the foothills of Himalayan range, mixed forests are found. Coniferous as well as deciduous types of forests are found in this region. Sal trees are seen in greater quantities in most of these forests.

(17) Deciduous forests of India.                       (March ’24)

Ans. (1) Deciduous forests are found in India in the areas receiving rainfall between 1000 mm and 2000 mm.

(2) Deciduous type of vegetation is characterised by trees that shed their leaves during dry/summer season.

(3) Trees like Teak, Bamboo, Banyan, Peepal, etc. are found in deciduous forests in India.

(4) Most of the forest area of India is covered by deciduous forests.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(12) Vegetation is scarce in the high altitude of Himalayas. (March ’23 – ’24)

Ans. (1) The temperature at high altitude of Himalayas is almost 0°C throughout the year. The area is almost snow covered for most of the days in year.

(2) Due to severe cold, vegetation do not grow in the high altitudes of Himalayas.

(3) During summer, the snow start melting and as its effect some seasonal flower trees grow in the higher altitude of Himalayas. These trees are extinct during winter. Therefore, vegetation is scarce in the high altitude of Himalayas.

(13) The northern part of Brazil is covered by dense forests. (July ’19)

Ans. (1) The amount of annual average rainfall is nearly 2000 mm in the northern part of Brazil. The annual average temperature of this region is about 28°C.

(2) The equator passes through the northern part of Brazil. Therefore, this region receives perpendicular sunrays throughout the year.

(3) Due to abundant sunshine and heavy rainfall, vegetation grow with high speed in this region. The life cycle and the density of vegetation is found to be high in this region. Therefore, the northern part of Brazil is covered by dense forests.

(14) Deciduous type of vegetation are found in India. (March ’22)

Ans. (1) Deciduous forests are found in the regions receiving rainfall between 1000 mm and 2000 mm.

(2) In most of the regions of India, the amount of rainfall is between 1000 mm and 2000 mm.

(3) Trees in deciduous forests, shed their leaves to maintain the minimum level of water. Thus, India has deciduous forests.

(15) Rainforests in Brazil are called the ‘lungs of the world’. (July ’22) OR The evergreen rainforests in Brazil are called the ‘lungs of the world’.                                        (March ’19; Sept. ’21)

Ans. (1) Rainforests are seen in the northern regions near the equator in Brazil.

(2) The trees in rainforests draw in carbon dioxide and breathe out oxygen.

(3) Thus rainforests help in providing us with most of our required oxygen and absorbing the carbon dioxide. Therefore, rainforests in Brazil are called the ‘lungs of the world’.

(16) A wide variety of species of insects is found in Brazil.

Ans. (1) Insects are mostly found in forests, grasslands and swampy lands.

(2) Many insects eat leaves, grass and nectar from the plant.

(3) The evergreen rainforests are seen in the northern parts of Brazil. The grasslands are found in the central parts and Paraguay- Parana river basin. Similarly, swampy lands are found in Pantanal region in Brazil. Therefore, a wide variety of species of insects is found in Brazil.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(23) What are the major causes of degradation of forests in Brazil and India?                                             (Nov. ’20)

In both Brazil and India, demand for settlement land leads to large-scale tree cutting. Roka farming in Brazil and jhum (zoom) agriculture in India clear forest for cultivation. Trees are also cut for firewood and other domestic needs.

(24) What environmental issues are faced by Brazil and India? (March ’25)

Ans. The following environmental issues are faced by Brazil and India :

(1) To fulfil the need of shelter of increasing population, for collecting firewood and for practising shifting cultivation trees are cut down on a large scale in both the countries. Therefore, Brazil and India facing a problem of deforestation.

(2) The problem of pollution is increasing in both the countries.

(3) Both the countries are facing a problem of environmental degradation due to increasing deforestation and pollution.

(4) Both the countries are facing a problem of extinction of many spices of vegetation and wildlife.

(25) Correlate wildlife and natural vegetation in India and Brazil.

Ans. (1) Natural vegetation is food of grazers/herbivores and many birds. Grazers/Herbivores are the food of carnivores.

(2) The regions having variety of natural vegetation also have variety of herbivores. As its effect, carnivores are also seen on a large scale in these areas.

(3) For example, deer are seen on a large scale in grasslands areas of Brazil. As its effect, Jaguar are also seen in large scale in this region.

(4) For example, insects in grass is food of Indian bustard. Therefore, Indian bustards are largely seen in the grasslands of India.

(5) Normally, variety of wildlife is seen in the areas with abundant natural vegetation.

(6) For example, abundant natural vegetation is found in the northern region near equator in Brazil. As its effect, variety of animals and birds are seen in this region.

(7) The lack of natural vegetation adversely affects the wildlife.

(8) For example, in Thar deserts in India the natural vegetation is limited. As its effect, extremely limited species of animals and birds are seen here.

(26) Explain the diversity of wildlife in Brazil.        (July ’23)

Ans. The diversity of wildlife in Brazil is explained with the help of the following points :

(1) Brazil is blessed with the rich wildlife. It has the highest diversity in the wildlife in the world.

(2) Huge anacondas are mainly found in the swampy areas of Pantanal. The animals like guinea pigs, crocodiles, alligators, monkeys, pumas, leopards, etc. are commonly seen in Brazil.

(3) Variety of fish is found in Brazil. Swordfish are mainly found in Atlantic Sea near Brazil. Pink dolphins and piranhas are mainly seen in rivers in Brazil.

(4) Huge sized condors that flow high in the sky are seen in Brazil. Various types of parrots, macaws, flamingoes are the other major birds as well as millions of varieties of insects are also found in Brazil.

(27) Why does the deciduous type of vegetation occupy most of India?

Ans. (1) Deciduous type of vegetation is characterised by trees that shed their leaves during dry/summer season.

(2) Shedding leaves decreases the rate of evaporation and it helps trees to conserve water and energy.

(3) Deciduous type of vegetation is found in the areas receiving rainfall between 1000 mm and 2000 mm.

(4) In most of India, the amount of annual average rainfall is between 1000 mm to 2000 mm. Therefore, the deciduous type of vegetation occupies most of India.

(28) Where do you find thorny and shrub vegetation in India? Why?

Ans. (1) Thorny and shrub vegetation is found in the state of Rajasthan and in the central part of peninsula.

(2) Most of region of Rajasthan and the central part of peninsula is included in a rain shadow area.

(3) The annual average rainfall received by these region is less than 500 mm.

(4) Thorny and shrub like vegetation is mainly grown in the areas experiencing hot summers and receiving less than 500 mm of rainfall. Therefore, thorny and shrub vegetation is found in Rajasthan and the peninsula.

notes.title: July 2024 Solved Paper, Assignment and July 2025 Practice Paper

July 2024 Board Paper — Q.7(3): What are the major causes of forest degradation in Brazil and India?

Ans. Both countries face pressure for land for human settlements, so trees are cleared. Roka farming in Brazil and jhum (called “Zoom” in the source) agriculture in India clear large forest areas for cultivation. Trees are also cut for firewood and other domestic needs.

Assignment — Q.7(4): State the major forest types in India and explain thorny and shrub-type vegetation.
